title: Globally generated sheaves on a regular surface point blowup have no H1
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $b:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. If $\mathcal F$ is generated by its global sections, meaning that the evaluation map $\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)}\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal F$ is surjective, then $H^1(Y,\mathcal F)=0$. Here $H^1$ is Zariski module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology].

proof.text: Apply the local chart package to $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and its reduced closed point $\mathfrak m$. Its hypotheses hold: regular-local localization makes $A$ a regular ring, so $T$ is regular by the definition; the spectrum-dimension equality gives $\dim T=2$. Any open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak m$ in $T$ is all of $T$: a principal open contained in that neighbourhood and containing $\mathfrak m$ is defined by an element outside $\mathfrak m$, hence by a unit. Also $A_{\mathfrak m}=A$, since all denominators are units. Thus the package's $Z$ is our $Y$, not a different base change. It gives nonzero parameters $s,t$ generating $\mathfrak m$, a domain $A$, and affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}C_s$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}C_t$ covering $Y$, with $C_s=A[\mathfrak m/s]$, $C_t=A[\mathfrak m/t]$. Their intersection $W$ is the basic open $D(t/s)$ in $U$ and $D(s/t)$ in $V$.

proof.text: Put $q=t/s\in C_s$. From the definition of a blowup chart, $C_s=A[q]\subseteq A_s$: for $a s+b t\in\mathfrak m$, its ratio by $s$ is $a+bq$, and $q$ itself is one generator. Likewise $C_t=A[p]\subseteq A_t$ with $p=s/t$. The basic-open section formula for the associated module, applied to the structure module, identifies $R=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Y)=C_s[q^{-1}]$. The package's $A$-algebra map $R\to A_{st}$ restricts on $C_s$ and $C_t$ to their inclusions into $A_{st}$. It is injective: $C_s\subseteq A_s\subseteq A_{st}$ because $A$ is a domain and $t\ne0$, and if $x/q^n$ ($x\in C_s$) maps to $0$ then $x$ maps to $0$, as $q$ maps to the unit $t/s$; so $x=0$. Both $p|_W\cdot q$ and $1$ map to $(s/t)(t/s)=1$, hence $p|_W=q^{-1}$ in $R$. Hence every $a\in R$ has a finite expression $\sum_{k=-N}^{M}a_kq^k$ with $a_k\in A$. Split this expression at $k=0$: its nonnegative terms are the restriction of $c=\sum_{k\ge0}a_kq^k\in C_s$, and its negative terms the restriction of $d=\sum_{k<0}a_kp^{-k}\in C_t$, since restriction is an $A$-algebra map. Consequently $a=c|_W+d|_W$. This is an additive decomposition; no uniqueness of the Laurent expression is asserted or needed.

proof.text: Write $I=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)$ and $P=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal O_Y$, with evaluation $e:P\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F$. For every affine open $B\subseteq Y$, restriction preserves this coproduct, and the affine tilde functor preserves coproducts and identifies their sections. Thus $P|_B\cong\widetilde{\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal O_Y(B)}$, with the canonical basis mapping under $e$ to $i|_B$. In particular $P$ is quasi-coherent and $\Gamma(B,P)=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathcal O_Y(B)$. Restriction preserves quasi-coherence of $\mathcal F$. These identifications apply to the affine $W$ of step 1. The restricted $e$ remains an epimorphism, since restriction preserves colimits, hence the cokernel presentation of an epimorphism.

Apply the quasi-coherent image theorem to $e|_W:P|_W\to\mathcal F|_W$. Its image sheaf is $\mathcal F|_W$ because $e|_W$ is an epimorphism, and its image on affine sections equals the sectionwise range. Therefore any $w\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal F)$ has an expression $w=\sum_{i\in J} a_i(i|_W)$ with $J\subset I$ finite and $a_i\in R$. Use step 2 to choose $a_i=c_i|_W+d_i|_W$. Set $u=-\sum_{i\in J}c_i(i|_U)$ and $v=\sum_{i\in J}d_i(i|_V)$. Since each $i$ is a single global section, its restrictions from $U$ and $V$ agree on $W$. Linearity now gives $v|_W-u|_W=w$. Thus the difference map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal F)\oplus\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal F)$ is onto.

proof.text: All nonempty repeated intersections in the two-member cover $(U,V)$ are $U,V,W$, hence affine. The affine-cover Cech comparison therefore computes $H^1(Y,\mathcal F)$. Explicitly a degree-one Cech cocycle has components $z_{00},z_{01},z_{10},z_{11}$; the equation $z_{jk}-z_{ik}+z_{ij}=0$ gives $z_{00}=z_{11}=0$ and $z_{10}=-z_{01}$. Step 4 gives $u,v$ with $v|_W-u|_W=z_{01}$. The degree-zero cochain $(u,v)$ then has differential $z$ on all four pairs. Every degree-one cocycle is a boundary, so $\check H^1((U,V),\mathcal F)=0$ and the comparison gives $H^1(Y,\mathcal F)=0$.
